prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Denver after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Denver for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you find the right Denver personal-injury lawyer — but I don’t have live web access from here to pull current phone numbers and up‑to‑date firm rankings. I can either (A) walk you through how to find and vet specific Denver firms right now, or (B) if you want, tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and I’ll build a short list for you that you can check online or call (and I’ll give exactly what to ask). Which do you prefer?

Meanwhile, here’s immediate, practical guidance so you can start calling firms today:

Which kinds of firms to call (and why)
- Large national/regional firms (e.g., Morgan & Morgan and similar): lots of resources, handle serious injuries and complex insurance fights, good if your case may involve major litigation.
- Local boutique trial firms: smaller teams that often handle fewer cases and can give more personalized attention and trial experience in Colorado courts.
- Solo or small-firm experienced car-accident attorneys: often lower overhead, direct attorney contact, good for straightforward claims.
- Firms that advertise contingency-fee representation and free consultations: you shouldn’t pay upfront; they are paid from any settlement or verdict.

Where to find vetted firms right now
- Colorado Bar Association and Denver Bar Association lawyer referral services.
- Super Lawyers (Colorado list), Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo — check ratings and client reviews.
- Look up recent verdicts/settlements in local news (indicates trial experience).
- Ask for recommendations from friends/family or your treating doctors.

What to have ready when you call
- Date/time/place of accident, police report number (if any), brief description of injuries and treatment, insurance info (yours and other drivers’), photos if available.

What to ask on the first call (short script)
- “Do you handle car-accident personal injury claims in Denver?” (If yes:) “How many of these cases have you handled in the last 3 years?” “What percent go to trial?” “Do you represent clients on contingency? What is your fee and are there other costs?” “Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?” “Can you give examples of recent settlements/verdicts for similar injuries?” “Do you have experience with my insurance company?” “What’s your expected timeline?” End: “Can I get a free consult or evaluation of my case?”

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount or outcome.
- Pushy hard-sell tactics or pressure to sign immediately.
- No willingness to provide references, past results, or clear fee agreement.
- Unclear contingency fee (standard is 33%–40%, sometimes more if case goes to trial).

How many to call
- Call 3–5 firms and compare answers, responsiveness, and whether you feel comfortable with the attorney.

If you want a tailored shortlist
- Tell me your Denver ZIP or the neighborhood of the accident, a short summary of injuries and whether the other driver was at fault/was ticketed, and I’ll prepare a recommended shortlist of firms to call plus exactly what to say to each and why I picked them (you’ll need to verify phone numbers locally or ask me to format the queries for online searching).

Which option would you like: immediate help with a shortlist, or step‑by‑step help searching and vetting on your own?
